name: Think-Aloud Protocol
description:
Think-aloud testing asks participants to verbalise what they are noticing, expecting and trying to do while interacting with a design. Their commentary is considered alongside observed behaviour to help researchers understand where expectations and interface behaviour diverge.

It is commonly used during usability evaluation.
whenToUse: Use think aloud when evaluating an interface or prototype and when understanding participants' interpretation of controls, content and feedback is important.
steps: Explain that the design rather than the participant is being evaluated.
Demonstrate the type of verbalisation requested if necessary.
Ask the participant to begin the task.
Observe behaviour without guiding them toward the solution.
Prompt them neutrally to keep talking if they become silent.
Record significant actions, comments and difficulties.
Analyse behaviour and verbal reports together.
lookOutFor: Thinking aloud changes the activity and can slow performance.
Participants cannot necessarily verbalise every cognitive process.
Avoid turning the session into an interview by asking explanatory questions during every action.

resources.citation: Ericsson, K. A. & Simon, H. A. (1993). *Protocol Analysis: Verbal Reports as Data*, rev. ed. MIT Press.
